To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

FedAvg achieves linear speedup in the number of devices for strongly convex and convex smooth problems, and for overparameterized linear problems, FedAvg can be accelerated to enjoy even faster speedup.
FedAvg has linear speedup in both strongly and convex problems, and that the Nesterov variant of FedAvg has linear convergence in strongly convex problems.

FedAvg enjoys a linear speedup in convergence with respect to the number of devices, with the exact convergence rate depending on the problem and the algorithmic choice, and we have provided a unified framework to analyze this linear speedup for a variety of settings.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the fundamental question of understanding the performance of FL algorithms in terms of the number of participants, and provides a comprehensive study of how FedAvg scales with the number and statistical heterogeneity of participating devices.
the fundamental convergence of FedAvg, and provides new insights into the convergence of FL.
a fundamental question of FL: how does convergence scale with the number of devices participating in the FL process?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the first time in the heterogeneous FL setting, we have provided the first linear speedups for FedAvg in all three classes of problems.
FedAvg enjoys a linear speedup in convergence with a constant factor of the number of participating clients.
FedAvg enjoys a linear speedup in all settings we considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the linear speedup property of FedAvg in FL is as strong as that of its counterpart in distributed optimization, which has been well-studied in the homogeneous setting.

, in all three problem classes, FedAvg has linear speedup in convergence rate, and the convergence rate of FedAvg can be accelerated by using momentum in the convex setting and by designing a new algorithm in the overparameterized setting.
FedAvg is provably efficient and effective for FL in both convex and non-convex settings.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, despite the heterogeneity and communication constraints, FedAvg can be made efficient by increasing the number of participating users, which is the opposite of the common belief that more users lead to slower convergence in federated learning.
, despite the non-iid data, the heterogeneity in the devices, and the limited participation, FedAvg enjoys the same speedup as distributed optimization with full participation.
FedAvg is an efficient FL algorithm that can be applied to a broad range of problems and enjoys linear speedup under both statistical and systems heterogeneity.
